decision: Start with the runtime identity spine because items 1, 2, 3, 6, and 7 share account/actor/lane/run/package/seam/worktree identity concerns and are likely to reduce downstream ambiguity across permissions, providers, capabilities, artifacts, and plan graph recovery.

decision: Use a shared `runtime_identity_envelope` with domain profiles as the runtime identity spine's organizing contract, rather than separate identity models per surface.

decision: Capability records must separate `enabled_on_instance` from `usable_now`; visible-but-unusable capabilities must carry `blocked_reason`, `caller_scope`, `execution_role`, and identity disclosure level.

decision: Artifact open-by-identity uses a stable `artifact_identity_ref` containing artifact identity, producer runtime identity, storage/version/digest identity, and FileManager open boundary semantics that avoid path-only identity.

decision: Expand the accepted runtime identity spine into per-owner ledger fix atoms now, before switching to Docker Manager active design or another cleanup cluster.

decision: Start Docker Manager active design with the `needs_review` vs failure-payload status/result contract before registry promotion, drift detection, access intelligence, and project-focused K8s linkage.
title: Start Docker active design with status/result contract

decision: Docker Manager uses a shared Docker operation result envelope where `needs_review` is non-terminal with review payload, and `failed` is terminal with failure payload.
title: Accept Docker operation result envelope semantics

decision: Docker operation result statuses are `pending`, `running`, `needs_review`, `succeeded`, `failed`, and `cancelled`; only `succeeded`, `failed`, and `cancelled` are terminal.
title: Accept Docker operation status enum

decision: Docker operation transitions are `pending -> running|cancelled`, `running -> needs_review|succeeded|failed|cancelled`, `needs_review -> running|failed|cancelled`, and no exits from `succeeded`, `failed`, or `cancelled`.
title: Accept Docker operation transition matrix

decision: Docker `review_payload` includes reviewer/actor identity, review reason, proposed action, required evidence, available actions, selected action, decision note, and resulting transition target.
title: Accept Docker review payload fields

decision: Docker `failure_payload` includes failure code/category, failing phase/status, human-readable message, evidence/log refs, retryability, remediation hint, affected target identity, and originating operation/transition context.
title: Accept Docker failure payload fields

decision: Docker registry promotion is a first-class Docker operation using the shared Docker operation result envelope, with a promotion payload carrying source image identity, target registry identity, digest/tag immutability, actor/runtime identity, policy gates, evidence refs, rollback/retry path, and promotion provenance.
title: Accept Docker registry promotion contract

decision: Docker drift detection is a first-class Docker operation using the shared Docker operation result envelope, with a drift payload carrying observed image/runtime identity, desired or pinned identity, diff category/severity, detection source/timestamp, policy impact, remediation options, evidence refs, acknowledgement/suppression scope, and promotion/rollback linkage.
title: Accept Docker drift detection contract

decision: Docker access intelligence is a first-class Docker operation/intelligence surface using the shared Docker operation result envelope, with an access payload carrying actor/runtime identity, account/project/worktree target identity, registry/resource identity, effective permission set, policy source, credential/secret boundary, risk classification, recommended action, evidence refs, audit provenance, and revocation/approval path.
title: Accept Docker access intelligence contract

decision: Docker project-focused K8s deep linkage is a first-class Docker/K8s integration operation using the shared Docker operation result envelope, with a linkage payload carrying project/worktree identity, cluster/context/namespace identity, workload identity, image/deployment identity, registry/promotion/drift refs, actor/runtime identity, permission boundary, rollout/rollback path, health/status refs, evidence refs, and cross-link navigation state.
title: Accept Docker project-focused K8s linkage contract
